negativity is a dominant force in the universe.

the general question of why negative entities are more powerful, and more varied, than positive ones, and how this bias is manifested in the cognitive, motivational, and social domains.
the nature and consequences of a general bias to give greater weight and attention to negative than to positive entities.
the question of why negative events have more impact than positive events.

negativity is the default state for human beings.

the negativity of the negative, the dominance of the negative, and the contagion of the negative, are the 3 key features of negative bias.

negativity bias, negativity dominance, and contagion are all part of a general negativity system, and that this system has evolved because it has been advantageous for animals and humans to be sensitive to negative entities in order to avoid harm and maximize survival.

negativity bias is a general phenomenon with a variety of manifestations.
negative entities, because of their potency, dominance and contagiousness, are more likely than positive entities to influence the course of human affairs.
